record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, let λ₁(Ω) be its first Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalue, and let Λ₁(Ω) be its first buckling eigenvalue. Must the scale-invariant product |Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)Λ₁(Ω) always be at least the n-ball value C_n^{4/n} j_{p,1}² j_{p+1,1}², where p = (n−2)/2?

evidence.quote: Another conjecture that suggests itself ... is |Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)Λ₁(Ω) ≥ [|Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)Λ₁(Ω)]|n-ball = C_n^{4/n} j²_{p,1} j²_{p+1,1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain with sufficiently smooth boundary, and let $|\Omega|$ denote its $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

Define $\lambda_1(\Omega)$ as the first eigenvalue of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the smallest $\lambda$ such that there exists a nontrivial $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with
$$-\Delta u=\lambda u\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$

Define $\Lambda_1(\Omega)$ as the first buckling eigenvalue of $\Omega$, i.e. the smallest $\Lambda$ such that there exists a nontrivial $u\in H_0^2(\Omega)$ with
$$\Delta^2 u=-\Lambda\Delta u\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=\partial_\nu u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$

Let $p=(n-2)/2$, and for $\nu\ge 0$ let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Let $C_n=\omega_n^{-2/n}\,j_{p,1}^{\,2}$ be the scale-invariant value of $|\Omega|^{2/n}\lambda_1(\Omega)$ when $\Omega$ is an $n$-ball, where $\omega_n$ is the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

Question: Does the inequality
$$|\Omega|^{4/n}\,\lambda_1(\Omega)\,\Lambda_1(\Omega)\;\ge\;C_n^{4/n}\,j_{p,1}^{\,2}\,j_{p+1,1}^{\,2}$$
hold for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, with equality when $\Omega$ is an $n$-ball?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not find a proof or disproof of the specific scale-invariant product inequality $|\Omega|^{4/n}\lambda_1(\Omega)\Lambda_1(\Omega)\ge C_n^{4/n}j_{p,1}^2 j_{p+1,1}^2$. Related conjectures (Payne's $\Lambda_1\ge\lambda_2$, Pólya–Szegő type bounds) are discussed in the literature, but the product conjecture itself appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Payne conjecture for Dirichlet and Buckling eigenvalues
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses inequalities between buckling and Dirichlet eigenvalues; product-type sharp bound not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related buckling/Dirichlet eigenvalue conjectures are still under active investigation, with no resolution of the product conjecture in question.

status_evidence.title: On the buckling eigenvalue problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style results on buckling eigenvalues and their bounds in terms of Dirichlet eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of the scale-invariant product inequality is recorded.
